title: Pick a model from professional brewhouse software
question: Four options modeled on professional brewhouse control software, all showing the same moment mid-mash with both pumps running. Pick one, or use the box to combine them. My suggestion: the process mimic (1) for the plumbing, with option 2's huge numbers and range bars, keeping colour for heat, pumps and alarms only.

options.label: 1: Brewhouse process mimic
options.lineage: The process pictures in brewhouse SCADA (Siemens BRAUMAT, WinCC)
options.thesis: Your rig drawn as it is plumbed: both pump loops, the coil in the HLT, a tag box of live values beside each vessel.
options.viewport: HLT, mash tun and boil kettle across the screen with the HLT-pump and wort-pump loops drawn; screen tabs on top; the current step and an event list at the bottom; clicking a device opens its faceplate.
options.risk: The temperatures in the tag boxes are too small to read across the garage, and tag numbers like P-201 are jargon until learned.
options.case: The most 'real brewhouse' of the four; the numbers need to grow before it meets your big-numbers rule.

options.label: 2: High-performance overview
options.lineage: ISA-101 high-performance HMI (as in Rockwell PlantPAx, Ignition templates)
options.thesis: Grey when things are normal, colour only when something needs you, and every temperature shown against its target band.
options.viewport: Three columns, one per vessel, each with a huge actual temperature, its setpoint, its own range bar, equipment rows and a 30-minute trend; alarms and the current step across the top.
options.risk: With no colour for normal running, an element that is on looks the same as a running pump, and the plumbing isn't shown.
options.case: The easiest to read from across the garage; the calm grey can under-sell the one thing that matters most, a live element.

options.label: 3: Batch board
options.lineage: Brewery batch control (BRAUMAT unit overview and graphical recipe, ISA-88)
options.thesis: One row per vessel with its step, time left, values and commands, beside the recipe as a numbered step chain.
options.viewport: Unit rows (HLT, mash tun, boil kettle) with state, step, time left, big actual and setpoint, equipment and Hold, Next step and Stop; the recipe's steps down the right with the active one highlighted.
options.risk: On hand-run days the step chain and step columns are empty, and it reads like a spreadsheet from a distance apart from the big numbers.
options.case: Best for recipe days and closest to mockup 03 you liked; the event list must stay a command log, not a brew record (BrewScribe's job).

options.label: 4: Brewhouse touch panel
options.lineage: The touchscreen in a craft brewhouse control cabinet (PanelView-style)
options.thesis: Chunky labelled buttons with lamp strips, big white-on-black readouts and screen tabs, like the panel on a 10-barrel brewhouse.
options.viewport: The three vessels drawn across the middle with big readouts under each, buttons stating HEATING 62 %, RUNNING or OFF, the step bar on top and tabs along the bottom.
options.risk: The rendered steel tanks are the hardest part to build well, and a dark screen fights your lit garage.
options.case: The most 'equipment' feel and the clearest buttons; the HERMS loop drawing in it is muddled and would need redrawing.

canonCard.label: The standard option (for comparison)
canonCard.thesis: What brewing-controller apps ship: vessel cards with toggles, a step list and a temperature chart, done well.
canonCard.viewport: Three vessel cards across the top, the recipe's steps on the right with Start, Next and Stop, and a two-hour temperature chart below.
canonCard.risk: Familiar and quick to build, but its toggles act on the first click (defect U2) and it is the generic-app look you said would feel wrong.
